default.summary: The human heart is a hollow, muscular organ that pumps blood through the circulatory system. It consists of four distinct chambers that separate oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

components.name: Left Ventricle
components.function: Pumps oxygen-rich blood to the entire body through the aorta under high pressure.
components.boardTip: Left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall among all 4 chambers.
components.funFact: Generates enough force to squirt blood up to 30 feet!

components.name: Right Ventricle
components.function: Pumps oxygen-depleted blood to the lungs via the pulmonary artery.
components.boardTip: Right side always handles DEOXYGENATED blood.
components.funFact: Pumps blood only to the nearby lungs, so its wall is thinner.

components.name: Atria (Left & Right)
components.function: Receiving chambers for blood returning from body organs and lungs.
components.boardTip: Atria push blood only down into the ventricles, requiring thin walls.
components.funFact: The word atrium comes from Latin meaning entrance hall.

components.name: Valves (Tricuspid & Bicuspid)
components.function: Flaps of tissue preventing backflow, keeping blood flowing in one direction.
components.boardTip: Bicuspid (Mitral) valve is on the Left; Tricuspid valve is on the Right.
components.funFact: The 'lub-dub' heart sound is caused by valves snapping shut.

default.deepDive: Double Circulation involves two separate circuits: Pulmonary (Heart -> Lungs -> Heart) and Systemic (Heart -> Body -> Heart). This double circulation prevents mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, giving warm-blooded animals high energy efficiency.
default.examTip:
✓ Draw a clean 4-box block diagram of the heart.
✓ Label Pulmonary Artery (carries deoxygenated blood) and Pulmonary Vein (carries oxygenated blood).
✓ Explain why ventricular walls are thicker than atrial walls.
default.realWorld: Artificial pacemakers are medical devices implanted when the SA node fails, producing rhythmic electrical signals to keep the heart beating.

child.summary: Your heart is a super energetic pump inside your chest that works 24/7 without taking any break!

components.name: Left Room (Ventricle)
components.function: Pushes fresh oxygenated blood all the way down to your toes!
components.boardTip: It's the strongest room in your heart!
components.funFact: It squeezes hard like a water squirt gun!

components.name: Right Room (Ventricle)
components.function: Sends tired blood back to your lungs so you can breathe fresh air.
components.boardTip: Sends blood right next door to the lungs.
components.funFact: Lungs recharge the blood with fresh oxygen!

child.deepDive: Think of your heart as a two-story house with 4 rooms. Blood comes in through the top rooms, drops to the bottom rooms, and gets launched out like a rocket!
child.examTip: Remember the heart has 4 rooms: 2 top and 2 bottom!
child.realWorld: Exercising makes your heart pump faster and stronger, just like running builds muscle in your legs!

board.summary: The human heart is a muscular organ enclosed in a double-walled membrane called pericardium, responsible for double circulation.

components.name: Sinoatrial (SA) Node
components.function: Acts as the natural pacemaker initiating electrical impulses for cardiac contraction.
components.boardTip: Located in the right atrium; frequently asked 1-mark question.
components.funFact: Fires around 70-80 impulse signals per minute.

components.name: Aorta
components.function: Largest artery carrying oxygenated blood from left ventricle to systemic arteries.
components.boardTip: High blood pressure inside aorta requires thick elastic walls.
components.funFact: The aorta is about the thickness of a garden hose.

board.deepDive: Double Circulation involves: 1) Pulmonary Circuit (Right Ventricle -> Pulmonary Artery -> Lungs -> Pulmonary Veins -> Left Atrium). 2) Systemic Circuit (Left Ventricle -> Aorta -> Body tissues -> Vena Cava -> Right Atrium).
board.examTip:
✓ Differentiate Arteries vs Veins (Wall thickness, Valves, Pressure).
✓ Define Pericardium and Pericardial Fluid function.
✓ Explain why double circulation prevents mixing of blood.
board.realWorld: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) is performed when blood vessels supplying the heart muscle become clogged.

hindi.summary: मानव हृदय एक मांसपेशीय अंग है जो पूरे शरीर में रक्त पंप करता है। इसमें चार कक्ष होते हैं जो ऑक्सीजन युक्त और ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त को अलग रखते हैं।

components.name: बायां निलय (Left Ventricle)
components.function: महाधमनी (Aorta) के माध्यम से पूरे शरीर में ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त पंप करता है।
components.boardTip: दाएं निलय की तुलना में बाएं निलय की दीवार अधिक मोटी होती है।
components.funFact: यह 30 फीट दूर तक रक्त छिड़कने जितना दबाव बना सकता है।

components.name: दायां निलय (Right Ventricle)
components.function: फुफ्फुस धमनियों के माध्यम से फेफड़ों में बिना ऑक्सीजन वाला रक्त भेजता है।
components.boardTip: दायां भाग हमेशा ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त संभालता है।
components.funFact: यह केवल पास के फेफड़ों तक ही रक्त पहुंचाता है।

hindi.deepDive: मानव में दोहरा परिसंचरण (Double Circulation) होता है। रक्त एक चक्कर पूरा करने के लिए हृदय से दो बार गुजरता है - एक बार फेफड़ों के लिए और दूसरी बार पूरे शरीर के लिए।
hindi.examTip:
✓ चार कोष्ठकों के चित्र का अभ्यास करें।
✓ धमनी और सिरा में अंतर याद रखें।
hindi.realWorld: पेसमेकर एक छोटा उपकरण है जो दिल की धड़कन को नियंत्रित करने के लिए छाती में लगाया जाता है।

hinglish.summary: Human heart ek powerful muscle pump hai jo poori body mein blood circulate karta hai. Isme 4 chambers hote hain taaki pure aur impure blood mix na ho.

components.name: Left Ventricle
components.function: Aorta ke through pure (oxygenated) blood poori body me pump karta hai.
components.boardTip: Dhyan do: Iski wall sabse thick hoti hai kyunki isse poori body me blood bhejna hota hai.
components.funFact: Iska pressure itna hota hai ki blood 30 feet door tak ja sakta hai!

components.name: Right Ventricle
components.function: Impure blood ko lungs me bhejta hai oxygen lene ke liye.
components.boardTip: Board tip: Right side matlab hamesha deoxygenated blood.
components.funFact: Lungs paas me hote hain, isliye iski wall thodi patli hoti hai.

hinglish.deepDive: Samjho ki Double Circulation kya hai! Blood heart me 2 baar aata hai. Pehle lungs se fresh oxygen lene, aur phir poori body ko dene ke baad wapas return hota hai.
hinglish.examTip:
✓ Board exam me 'Double Circulation' ka 3-mark Question pakka aata hai!
✓ Lub-Dub sound valves band hone par hoti hai.
hinglish.realWorld: Jab kisi ki heart rate bohot slow ho jaati hai, toh doctors Artificial Pacemaker lagate hain.

mcq.summary: Check your understanding of Cardiac Anatomy through these practice MCQs.

components.name: Q1: Which chamber pumps blood to the entire body?
components.function: Option A: Right Atrium | Option B: Left Ventricle (Correct) | Option C: Right Ventricle | Option D: Left Atrium
components.funFact: Left Ventricle needs maximum muscle force to push blood to distal organs.

components.name: Q2: What is the primary function of Heart Valves?
components.function: Option A: Produce oxygen | Option B: Prevent backflow of blood (Correct) | Option C: Increase blood pressure | Option D: Filter blood
components.funFact: Valve closure causes the Lub-Dub heartbeat sound.

mcq.deepDive: Solve multiple choice questions to strengthen concept clarity for board examinations.
mcq.examTip: Read options carefully before selecting. Eliminate wrong choices first.
mcq.realWorld: Medical entrance tests like NEET heavily emphasize MCQ practice.

default.summary: The human brain is the central control unit of the nervous system, responsible for thought, memory, emotion, touch, motor skills, and regulating body processes.

components.name: Cerebrum
components.function: Responsible for high-level thinking, memory, intelligence, and voluntary actions.
components.boardTip: Largest part of the brain; divided into left and right hemispheres.

components.name: Cerebellum
components.function: Controls posture, balance, precision, and muscular coordination.
components.boardTip: Known as the 'little brain' located at the base of the skull.
components.funFact: Alcohol affects the cerebellum first, causing loss of physical balance.

components.name: Medulla Oblongata
components.function: Controls involuntary reflexes such as breathing, heart rate, swallowing, and blood pressure.
components.boardTip: Part of the hindbrain connecting directly to the spinal cord.
components.funFact: Damage to the medulla is almost instantly fatal.

default.deepDive: The brain is protected by 3 layer membranes called meninges and cushioned by Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF). It consumes nearly 20% of the body's total oxygen supply.
default.examTip:
✓ Label Forebrain, Midbrain, and Hindbrain correctly.
✓ Remember: Cerebrum = Voluntary/Thinking, Cerebellum = Balance, Medulla = Involuntary.
default.realWorld: Electroencephalography (EEG) measures electrical activity in the brain to diagnose epilepsy and sleep disorders.

default.summary: The cell is the basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all known organisms.

components.name: Mitochondria
components.function: Generates cellular energy in the form of ATP through cellular respiration.
components.boardTip: Always referred to as the 'Powerhouse of the Cell'.
components.funFact: Mitochondria have their own independent DNA and ribosomes.

components.name: Nucleus
components.function: Contains genetic material (DNA) and controls all cellular activities.
components.boardTip: Acts as the command center or 'Brain of the Cell'.
components.funFact: Red blood cells in mammals mature without a nucleus to carry more oxygen.

default.deepDive: Eukaryotic cells contain membrane-bound organelles while prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles.
default.examTip:
✓ Compare Plant Cell vs Animal Cell (Cell Wall, Vacuoles, Plastids).
✓ Define Diffusion and Osmosis clearly.
default.realWorld: Stem cell research allows scientists to grow organ tissues to cure degenerative diseases.
